correctness.rationale: Parseval gives an exact sum over ordered representations as two positive squares. All weights are strictly positive, making congruence of phases for every equal-square sum necessary and sufficient. The six character functions satisfy these relations by the explicitly disjoint residues modulo 16, the count modulo 3, and the unique 0+0 versus 1+4 collision modulo 5. Their initial 6x6 determinant is exactly 120. Five verified two-square identities determine phases 7 to 11; for every k>=12 the explicit integer 3-4-5 rotation gives a,b,c<k and k²+a²=b²+c², forcing all remaining phases inductively. Only three relations through N=10 establish the 7-dimensional predecessor. The included standard-library checker verifies ranks, modular identities, arithmetic descent, and direct fourth moments; these do not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Finite fourth-moment majorants for polynomial Fourier spectra are central to recent harmonic-analysis norm research. A routine triangle inequality alone leaves all equality phases completely unresolved: here the positive squares exhibit four additional, genuinely arithmetic continuous symmetries beyond global phase and translation. The result gives a complete classification uniform over arbitrary positive coefficient magnitudes, an exact parameter-cover degree 120, and the surprising sharp cutoff N=11 after a nonmonotone small-size phase dimension. The cutoff and modular characters are motivated by the natural full equality-in-majorant problem rather than by arbitrary parameter slices.
